info.name: account-updater v1.2.0
info.description: Checks whether a repo meets the eligibility requirements to connect an account. Repo references on github, gitlab, bitbucket are recognized and evaluated.

item.name: Liveness check: is this process alive?
Readiness check: are this instance's dependencies usable?

request.description: Distinct from /health, which only reports that the process is alive. Returns 503 when the cache backend or the SQLite audit trail is unreachable - both are non-fatal per request by design (a cache error degrades to a miss, an audit write failure is swallowed), so a load balancer has no other way to see them.

item.name: In-memory operational counters for this process
Prometheus text-exposition-format view of the same counters as GET /metrics
Which forges this build recognizes and can evaluate

request.description: For a client deciding what it may send: the forges this service knows how to name, which of them are actually evaluated, and what a reference to each looks like. Assembled from the same tables the request path uses, so it cannot claim support the service does not have. Says nothing about which credentials are configured - that is an operator's question, answered by `npm run doctor`.

item.name: The thresholds a repo is measured against

request.description: The eligibility bar as this build enforces it: the size, history, and active-development thresholds, the signal weights behind the blended active-development score, and which languages count. Served from the same values the checks read, so it cannot drift from what a check will do. The `fingerprint` identifies the rule set - it is what cached verdicts are namespaced by, so two results carrying the same one were decided by the same rules.

item.name: Evaluate up to 20 repos in one request

request.description: A convenience for callers holding a list, not a way around the rate limit: the request spends one unit of the /eligibility budget per repo listed, because each one is cloned and checked against the provider API individually.

item.name: Read-only view of the evaluation audit trail

query.description: "owner/name" or a repo URL - when omitted, lists the most recent evaluations across all repos. Filtering is scoped to the reference's provider as well as its owner/repo.
Restrict to evaluations that passed (true) or failed (false). Omit for both.
Inclusive lower bound on when the evaluation happened, as an ISO-8601 timestamp. An unparseable value is a 400, not an empty result.
Inclusive upper bound, same format as `since`.

request.description: Lists past evaluations from the SQLite audit trail, most recent first. Filters combine: `repo` for one repo, `eligible` for outcome, `since`/`until` for a time window, and `limit` to cap the result count (default 50, max 200).

item.name: Aggregate view of the evaluation audit trail

query.description: Summarize one repo instead of all of them.
Inclusive lower bound on the window, as an ISO-8601 timestamp.
Inclusive upper bound, same format as `since`.
How many failure-reason groups to return.

request.description: Counts over a window rather than the rows themselves: how many evaluations, how many passed, across how many distinct repos, and which failures came up most often. Failure reasons carry per-repo specifics (counts, language names), so they are grouped with those parts replaced - `Only N lines of first-party source found (need at least N).` - with one verbatim example per group. The reason tally reads at most the 2000 most recent failures in the window; `reasonsSampled` says how many it actually read.
